topic: TNF and IL-17 inhibitors in axSpA: secukinumab, ixekizumab, comparative efficacy
synopsis: This pharmacology review treats TNF inhibitors as a well-established first-line biologic option in ankylosing spondylitis, with long-term data and efficacy for extra-articular disease such as uveitis and inflammatory bowel disease. It describes IL-17 inhibitors as providing comparable efficacy for axial disease, with a particular advantage when psoriasis is significant or tuberculosis risk is increased. A Cochrane review it cites found that patients on anti-TNF therapy were about three to four times more likely than placebo patients to reach ASAS40 by 6 months. Secukinumab was the first IL-17A inhibitor approved for ankylosing spondylitis. In MEASURE 1 and 2, ASAS20 at week 16 was approximately 60–61% with secukinumab 150 mg and 75 mg versus 29% with placebo, and ASAS40 was approximately 28–36% versus 11%. In COAST-X, ixekizumab 80 mg every 4 weeks or every 2 weeks produced ASAS40 rates of 35–40% at week 16 versus 19% with placebo in non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, which supported approval for active non-radiographic disease with objective inflammation.

teachingPoints.claim: TNF inhibitors are a first-line biologic with extra-articular efficacy; IL-17 inhibitors have comparable axial efficacy.
